claim: SR-Eval decomposes code generation into sequential, evolving requirement turns via a multi-agent simulation pipeline and semantic-aware discriminative test-case generation, spanning 443 multi-turn tasks and 1,857 questions at function and repository level across Python and Java.
stance_target: existing requirement-decomposition benchmark designs for code LLMs
scope_conditions: Python and Java, function-level and repository-level tasks
quoted_support: SR-Eval comprises 443 multi-turn tasks and 1,857 questions at both function and repository levels.

claim: SR-Eval's requirement decomposition is temporal/sequential (successive multi-turn refinement of one evolving requirement) rather than concurrent decomposition of a single static task into co-existing sub-requirements tested by separate unit-test methods.
stance_target: distinction between multi-turn requirement-refinement benchmarks and concurrent per-requirement/unit-test partial-credit benchmarks
quoted_support: developers seldom work from a complete requirement; instead, requirements are incrementally refined through successive iterations of development.
